neighbours.label: the split word-start fragment ' fl' / ' bl' when the word continues with something other than a common whole word (fl|aky, fl|apping, bl|ared, fl|imsy)
fire: The croissant had a flaky crust and a soft middle.
We heard the flapping of a loose sail in the wind.
Car horns blared in the street below the hotel.
The shed had a flimsy door that rattled all night.
He blurted the secret before she could stop him.
The goose flapped its wings and chased the dog.
Old paint was flaking off the kitchen ceiling.
A radio was blaring from the open garage.
quiet: The croissant had a flat crust and a soft middle.
We heard the flag of a ship snapping in the wind.
Car horns sounded in the street below the hotel.
The shed had a black door that rattled all night.
He blamed the secret on her before she could speak.
The goose flew over the fence and chased the dog.
Old paint lay on the floor under the kitchen ceiling.
A blue radio was playing in the open garage.

notes: Probes: ' bl'(ared) 0.85, ' fl'(aky) 0.75, ' fl'(apping) 0.70, ' fl'(imsy) 0.36, ' bl'(urted) 0.28, ' flo'(pped) 0.20, ' flav'(oured) 0.18; whole-token words flash, flag, black, fluttering near 0. Card also lists ' trans' and one ' first', not tested ('transpose' 0.02). The output suppresses 'flash', ' bl', ' gl', and the - pole fires on ' gl'(itzy), ' br'(asher), so the unit seems to sort which fl-/bl- word is coming.
